Remove duplicated success manufacture from the value-returning helper; no root slot, runtime record, allocation or representation field added

gerbil-bootstrap-module-custody

Unchanged per-module source/options/parent/runtime and exact output bytes require the immutable same-run completed process witness; queued, partial, failed or unknown outputs never qualify. Child records do not become recipe-stage PASS. Publication is serialized while independent compiler processes overlap within a host-derived envelope.

Reuse165 authenticated completed bootstrap modules in one owned source workspace; avoid full Git archive/extract for a pinned empty overlay after normal source-checkpoint validation; remove serial scheduling of independent stage0 compiler actions.
gerbil-resource-and-source-context

The existing managed source delta preserves caller runtime options before authoritative install mappings. Source overlays enter action identity rather than the physical workspace key. Only a target matching its previous witnessed input may be replaced. Compiler semantic context includes GAMBOPT; independent-action job capacity does not change it. Parent plus J one-processor compiler jobs uses a conservative 2J+1 scheduling envelope, not an OS-thread quota.

No new checkout for a managed source delta; unchanged input copies retain timestamps. Exact completed-module outputs can be reused after validation. No automatic multiplication by the host default processor population.
callback-nonlocal-exit-custody

A throw from ___call carries explicit control origin through both SFUN sites. All three generated families skip conversion recovery for thrown control, execute existing cleanup and propagate the unchanged status. Declarations and function-table signatures migrate with the wrappers. Reaching a Scheme continuation can precede physical C return: still-active callback banks remain roots across GC until their own unwind. Never restore an obsolete Scheme frame or prematurely drop its bank.
Retire raw ___call returns that bypass the generated cleanup boundary; do not weaken teardown refusal or discard retained roots.
unpublished-stage1-lookup-custody

Only a completed matching stage1 proof may remain in the consumer lookup path. Before retrying an unqualified stage1, leased and quiescent ownership permits withdrawing its core/static outputs and Gerbil launchers by inode move into the attempt evidence directory. Preserve completed bootstrap and Gambit runtime payloads. Never overwrite retained failed custody or move outputs of an unknown live producer.
Avoid retrying bootstrap from a loader polluted by previously failed frontend output; keep completed stage0 products and the same physical source workspace
generated-host-compilation-unit

The existing profile single-host=0 enables single-host with no label-count limit; zero does not disable it. Compile-unit structure, frontend generation and independent-action scheduling are distinct responsibilities. Any proposed host partition must preserve PointId/FrameSpec, cross-host tail transfer, root maps and multi-shot continuation interpretation rather than changing a test's acceptance context.
No removal claimed yet. Structural host partitioning must be justified on the generator/runtime chain; neither extra Make jobs nor C23 itself splits one host function
compiler-job-budget

Qualified native core compiler actions start one Scheme processor per Make job. Initial processor sum <= active jobs <= J; configured target Scheme SMP features are unchanged. This is not an OS-thread quota or a claim about arbitrary effectful compile-time code or interpreted compiler adapters
Retire nested J-by-host-processor initial populations and idle participant/GC coordination in the admitted native core path
target-feature-dependency

One existing Configure source exports the target prelude and generation options into its existing feature header; module C depends on that header. C source edits do not change it; configuration changes cannot silently reuse unqualified generated C
Remove implicit feature selection from timestamp-only module reuse; retire hand-maintained derived bodies as semantic authority

content-stable-stamp

generated-publication-family

Default publication and configured SMP outputs carry distinct target-feature and source-location contexts. Changed Scheme/native embedded bodies regenerate their default C and all downstream descriptors. Never copy profile-specific SMP C over default publication or normalize observable source paths away

GerbilModuleBuild::execution and existing toolchain resource obligations
Existing runtime_roles.qnt frozen-origin and participant premises; initialization is a C source refinement, not another schedule or Lean theorem
Existing Scheme primitive specialization contract and native counterexamples; no duplicate QNT or Lean scheduler

Seven real source routes and27 anchors locate root publication, RC scanning, task completion, R-context restoration before owner cleanup, join-dependent still transfer and retained-state cleanup refusal. These are conditional source observations, not complete C memory-order or stopped-writer proofs. Supported synchronous lifetime and changed callers must close in this REV; independent carrier retirement, universal foreign recovery, collector generations and frontend performance remain later programme work.

Conditional source counterexample: cleanup_vmstate may refuse a retained secondary VM through a void return, while global cleanup has no returned refusal receipt and continues to global resource teardown. A complete VM-registry/admission and acknowledgement protocol must precede irreversible global teardown; a racy preflight check alone is insufficient. Native secondary-VM reachability is not yet established. This remains M-REFINE/Q-FAILURE/Q-LIFETIME, not a frontend optimization or an admitted failure-recovery result.
One configured public gambit.h, byte-identical to ordered concatenation; private source modules live under include/_gambit; no extra runtime includes or ABI aliases

This REV must migrate its changed SFUN/RC/Tcl generator, declarations, function tables, definitions and callers together, preserving Scheme control/root/resource/error semantics. Internal C APIs and layouts may be replaced. Existing binary ABI/layout stability is not a default requirement; old artifacts must be rebuilt or positively rejected under their actual admission rules. Universal foreign-thread admission and redesigned CFFI/destructor services are later cuts; touched-consumer safety remains mandatory.

The parent SMP twelve-gate inventory, generational collector, independently retiring worker/carrier, universal foreign ownership and matched release performance are programme goals, not a demand that one REV implement the entire modernization. Current REV requirements are selected by its touched consumers, stated claims and dependencies; missing applicable tests cannot be waived.

Original379 assertion bodies and PR fixtures stay unchanged. Bounded p3 and p2 compiled observations remain incomplete. The shared-support and byte-order experiments failed to establish whole-inventory closure and are retired. Complete current GSI/GSC native inventories remain separate mandatory checks.

The actual new mainline bootstrap37aaf01a completed in the same SDK in309.042215 seconds. Existing Configure was reused with51 generated files unchanged. A new immutable mainline-runtime bootstrap reference binds1228 core inputs and the real producer/map/verdict consumer passed. The first export path rejection and stale process-observation engine rejection remain retained. Only the framework transport seal was renewed against its exact tested implementation; native bootstrap identities and ancestry checks were not weakened. Historical producer references retain their original scope.

Preserve Scheme observable evaluation, exception and dynamic-wind behaviour, proper tail calls, shared object identity and multi-shot continuation/GC restoration; effects may be extended explicitly without silently weakening these guarantees.

Replace internal PSTATE/carrier bindings, frame/root representations, C helper signatures, function tables, ownership and allocation protocols as complete producer/consumer migrations. No duplicate namespace, alias or compatibility facade is required.

A rebuilt generator/header/runtime/module cohort is the default migration. Unrebuilt old binary extensions are not promised to load. setup.c currently checks compiler version and selected structure sizes; this is not a complete same-size layout or function-signature fingerprint. Reject or rebuild uncertain artifacts; a size check alone is not admission.

Keep unchanged GSC300 and numeric90 limits and the existing profile. single-host=0 is unlimited single-host, not disabled. The8008-label/5.60MB module finishes generation then times out in native construction; preprocessing alone1.98s/21.49MB does not account for the whole phase. Structural host partition must preserve PointId/FrameSpec/tail/root/multi-shot contracts, not tune a test threshold.

Full current-runtime producer/consumer qualification and runtime-ABI invalidation remain open; no new source copy was created.

Text and binary table decoders share strong construction roots before committing weak/index flags and reconstruction debt. Real roundtrip plus concurrent GC and explicit between-store GC controls pass on the new bootstrap. This closes an observed construction window, not all GC/FFI root producers or native stop recovery.

Safe vector-inc specialization must check vector, mutability, index, increment and existing element before the unsafe atomic fetch-add. Checks short circuit before vector-ref and preserve the Scheme fallback and old-value result. Original invalid-delta assertion and independent invalid-element/no-write controls pass; no concurrent arbitrary-type mutation claim.
